title: Same 36-cell block, two body colours: is the smudge the shape or the colour?
question: Which of these is closer to reading as a creature? If neither, say which of the two is the bigger problem - the outline or the colour.
context_md:
You said of the last pair: *"Both are smudges but A is closer."* That could mean two things and they call for opposite work, so here is the other one isolated.

**Identical body**, cell for cell -- the same 3x3 plan at double density, 36 cells, 6x6 on the grid. The **only** difference is the material the flesh is made of, and both already exist in the repo.

Zoomed to 28 px per physical unit, so this is much closer than play scale: at play scale each of these is a 6-pixel-wide object.

The previous pair varied the *outline* at fixed colour and you picked the waisted one. This pair varies the *colour* at fixed outline. Between the two answers I can tell whether the next work is a better silhouette or a better palette -- and `plant-appearance-design.md` is the warning that it is usually the palette, since a lever that relabels a cell cannot move a silhouette that texture and colour set.
